context.body: Then the LORD’s angel commanded Gad to tell David that David should go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

context.body: Succession, Retelling, and Temple Preparation · 1 Chronicles 21:18–30
context.label: Canonical location

observations.body: The angel directs Gad, David buys the place for six hundred gold shekels, builds an altar, receives fire from heaven, sees the sword sheathed, and fears to go to Gibeon.
observations.label: Fire answers at Ornan’s threshing floor: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps The angel, Gad, David, Ornan, Ornan’s sons, and the LORD, Ornan’s threshing floor, Jerusalem, and Gibeon, directing, threshing, hiding, buying the place, building, sacrificing, answering by fire, sheathing, and fearing visible within David's story or later memory.

observations.body: The angel, Gad, David, Ornan, Ornan’s sons, and the LORD · Ornan’s threshing floor, Jerusalem, and Gibeon · directing, threshing, hiding, buying the place, building, sacrificing, answering by fire, sheathing, and fearing · the purchased place becomes an altar site and the reason David remains there

payload.posture: Read 1 Chronicles 21:18–30 as its own succession, retelling, and temple preparation David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places the purchased place becomes an altar site and the reason David remains there inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
